text:
Sam: heads-up — increased user reports from eu-west that long-running chat sessions drop after ~70s, clients see premature EOF on gRPC streaming.
Elaine: :eyes: seeing any consistent server-side logs? RST_STREAM or GOAWAY?
Sam: clients: "stream closed by remote (premature EOF)". On our side envoy shows stream reset with error code 2 then connection stays open.
Nora: ALB metrics show a bunch of 504/502 from the target group right when drops spike. Idle timeout shows 60s in ALB config.
Matt: timeline: client opens long-lived HTTP/2 -> ALB -> envoy(edge) -> backend. Could be idle timeout on an intermediate hop + connection reuse.
Sam: captured tcpdump from a host during repro, snippet:
```
12:05:22.987 IP client->alb: TCP 443 [PSH, ACK]
12:06:33.214 IP alb->edge: FIN, ACK
12:06:33.215 IP edge->backend: RST
```
Elaine: so ALB is closing around ~70s despite idle configured 60s? jitter from health checks or intermittent small gaps in traffic could trigger idle detection.
Nora: envoy logs show this pattern too:
```
[2026-03-17T12:06:33.215Z] [warning] stream reset: stream_id=15, reason=CLIENT_RESET
[2026-03-17T12:06:33.216Z] [info] connection remained open, new streams accepted
```
Matt: interesting that connection remains open but stream reset happens. Could be edge proxy applying per-stream flow control clamp when WINDOW_UPDATE frames are lost/blocked by ALB buffering.
Sam: also noticed our egress NAT hosts had a spike in ephemeral port churn during the incident window (many short-lived mappings). Not full exhaustion but high churn.
Elaine: hypothesis: ALB or infra middlebox is buffering HTTP/2 frames, then cutting the stream when it sees inactivity; edge/envoy sees partial/garbled frames -> RST_STREAM, but underlying TCP stays since keepalives between ALB and edge still active.
Nora: can we repro with debug capture that includes HTTP/2 frame logs on envoy + ALB access logs? I can correlate timestamps if we enable extra tracing.
Sam: already did one capture — attaching timeline in thread. Repro steps are simple: start a streaming chat, let it idle ~65s with only periodic tiny client pings. We see drop ~67-72s.
Matt: mitigation options:
- increase ALB idle timeout to 300s (quick config change)
- enable TCP-level keepalive between ALB and edge (if supported)
- change ALB target type to instance vs ip? (affects connection reuse)
- add periodic application-level ping frames over the stream
Elaine: long term we should make edge more defensive: accept short gaps without resetting streams when connection still healthy, and log h2 frame parsing failures more verbosely.
Nora: also check whether our NAT gateway is doing port-preserving ephemeral reuse that confuses ALB session tracking. If port reassignment happens mid-stream, ALB may decide backend is dead and inject GOAWAY.
Sam: quick plan: 1) prod ramp: increase ALB idle to 300s in eu-west canary 2) enable more verbose envoy h2 debug on a subset 3) correlate tcpdump + ALB logs for next 2 hours 4) add client ping in SDK as short-term workaround.
Matt: +1, do the change during low traffic window. I'll own the ALB change and rollback plan.
Elaine: pushing a small envoy config change to enable "h2 debug frames" on canary cluster, Nora will collect.
infra-bot: Scheduled: ALB idle-timeout increase for tg-eu-west canary at 2026-03-17T23:00Z by Matt. Monitor window 90m.
Nora: will start tracing correlator and post logs here. If anyone sees new failures after the change ping me.
Sam: thanks all — leaning toward ALB timeout being the gating factor plus some edge parsing fragility. Will keep thread updated with traces. :thumbsup:
